A fermentation jar of dark stoneware sealed with cloth and twine on the bottom shelf, its sides filmed with condensation, a paper label in cramped script reading the contents and a date four years past.

A reading-glass case of scarred black leather resting open on the mantle-shelf, one glass still inside, the other absent, the velvet interior impression of the missing glass still visible as a shallow oval in the lining.

A low oak worktable with a rune-carved border along its apron, its surface cross-hatched with knife-marks, ink-stains, and burn-rings, one corner reinforced with an iron bracket bolted on after some past structural disagreement.

A beetle-pinned wall display in a shallow frame, forty-six specimens arranged by wing-color from pale amber to deep black, the forty-seventh pin empty, its label still reading: PENDING CAPTURE — MARSH EXPEDITION.

A pewter dish of charm-stones on the window ledge, nine smooth river-pebbles each inscribed with a single rune in iron-gall ink, arranged in a pattern that suggests intent but whose meaning the arrangement itself refuses to clarify.

A binding-knot rope coil hanging on a wall peg, its cord dyed in alternating bands of black and grey, one end terminating in a knot of formidable complexity, the other end simply cut and left unfinished.

A fossilized rune-stone in a padded case lined with green cloth, the stone itself deep grey with ochre inclusions, the carved rune on its face worn half-smooth but its outline inked over in fresh black to preserve legibility.
A copper still-head sitting in a wooden cradle, its spout plugged with a cork painted red, a luggage-tag wired to the handle reading: DO NOT USE WITH SULFUR COMPOUNDS — THIRD TIME ASKING.

A mounted dragon-eye in a jar of preserving fluid on a high shelf, its vertical pupil still visibly slit even in death, the jar labeled in a careful hand: YEAR ACQUIRED UNKNOWN — PROVENANCE COMPLICATED.
A brass magnifying lens in a hinged case of cracked leather, its handle wrapped in fraying cord, one edge of the glass chipped in a small arc that has been circled with a grease mark and dated.

A leather footstool beside the armchair, its top surface creased and shiny with use, one brass tack missing from the corner so the fabric pulls free and shows the dry horsehair stuffing packed beneath.

A sigil-burned door-jamb wedge of dark oak, its flat face carved with a ward-glyph and scorched around its edges as though the inscription generated its own heat during application, one corner charred entirely black.

A preserved scaled claw in a glass-topped specimen case, its scales still holding an iridescent blue-green despite obvious age, the small printed label beside it bearing only three words: NOT FROM HERE.

A warded lockbox of black iron on the floor beside the chest, its lid secured with three different lock mechanisms of incompatible designs, a knotted length of cord threaded through all three hasps as a final, deeply human precaution.
A squat copper alembic crouched on a soot-blackened trivet, its neck wrapped in asbestos cord gone grey with use, a single amber droplet perpetually forming at the spout's tip but never falling.
An iron-banded retort resting in a sand-bath, its glass belly stained deep ochre from decades of sulfur work, its cork stopper branded with the word VOLATILE in uneven capitals.

A coiled distilling serpent of green-tinted glass clamped to a wooden rack, each loop furred with mineral deposit, the lowest curve still holding a finger's worth of something that glows faintly rose.
A wide-mouthed fermentation jar sealed with beeswax and linen, its contents a murky sage-green, a strip of vellum tied to the neck reading only: third batch — do not taste until Solstice.
A tarnished brass still-head wedged between two leaning books, its soldered seams repaired three times over in progressively cruder work, a dry herb-bundle stuffed inside to keep the smell contained.
A shallow herb-press of aged rosewood, its two boards held by iron wing-screws gone orange with rust, a sprig of dried wormwood still caught in the hinge, flattened translucent as onion skin.
A ceramic oil-extractor missing its lower spigot, plugged instead with a whittled birch dowel wrapped in waxed thread, its glaze crazed into a map-like network of fine brown lines.
A stone mortar worn smooth and cream-pale at the bowl's center, its pestle handle darkened where a thumb has worn the grain to glass, a residue of violet powder dried hard around the rim.

A glass condenser suspended between two brass clamps, one end sealed with a blown-glass bulb the size of a fist, its interior laced with hairline cracks that catch the candlelight into brief prismatic stars.

An open grimoire propped on a reading stand, its left page blazing with self-illuminating crimson script, the right page blank but visibly scorched at the margins, the binding cracked and re-glued twice over.

A leather-bound codex splayed face-down to hold a page, its spine split along two inches and mended with a strip of darker leather that doesn't quite match, a pressed moth forgotten between pages forty and forty-one.
A vellum scroll-case of pale ivory tube, its end-cap sealed with red wax stamped with a coiled drake, a handwritten label along the side reading: survey — eastern ridge — not authoritative.

A palimpsest sheaf held flat under a chunk of green tourmaline, the older text bleeding through in ghost-brown beneath the newer ink, two words circled in the underlayer and connected by a faint scratched line.

A reading-glass case of cracked brown leather, its brass latch sprung so it rests perpetually half-open, the glass inside ground with a slight astigmatism that bends text toward the upper-right corner.

A bound stack of illuminated manuscript pages tied with faded blue ribbon, one page turned outward to show a marginalia dragon sketched in iron-gall ink, its tail curling into the decorated initial of the main text.

A rack of stoppered amber bottles in descending height, three glowing faintly amber, one sealed with black wax stamped with a dragon sigil, the smallest bottle empty but for a single iridescent scale the size of a fingernail.

A specimen jar of blown green glass holding a preserved root, its label water-stained to illegibility except for a large red exclamation painted below the text, the cork pressed down and additionally sealed with candle-wax.

A row of dropper-bottles in a cedarwood tray, each stopper color-coded with a daub of paint, the red-stoppered one missing its dropper-tube entirely and stuffed instead with a rolled scrap of instructions.

A sealed wax-stamped vessel of dark pottery, its stamp showing three concentric rings pressed by a signet, resting in a nest of woodchip packing inside a cracked wooden box labeled: DO NOT OPEN INDOORS.

A vial rack holding fourteen thin glass tubes, five capped with stretched pig-bladder tied with twine, one tube deliberately inverted and wedged between its neighbors to prevent the contents from settling.

A crystal orb on a three-legged brass tripod, its surface clouded at one pole by an interior flaw the size of a walnut, its base-ring engraved with a lunar calendar, its needle perpetually restless rather than settling.
A scrying bowl of hammered copper, its interior coated in a resin that holds a mirror-black sheen even dry, a thumbprint pressed into the rim's patina and never polished away.

A tarot deck in a silk sleeve gone grey-green with handling, three cards dog-eared at corners, the top card lying face-up beside the sleeve showing a tower struck by drawn lightning with a red ink question mark added in the margin.

A brass astrolabe hanging from a wall-hook on a leather thong, its arc engraved with constellation names worn shallow, a single dried ink-mark on the index arm indicating a position never corrected back to zero.
